title: Large Bricks and Join-irreducible torsionfree classes

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof takes a spanning tree T of the underlying graph of the Hasse quiver, chooses a module for each vertex and a non-zero map for each edge, and then asserts: "This gives a directed system of f−simples consisting of monomorphisms (we don't have any compatibility condition to check on the maps as the underlying graph is a tree), therefore we can use Lemma 3.6". A tree-shaped diagram inside the Hasse quiver is precisely NOT a directed (filtered) system: the edges of the spanning tree point in arbitrary directions, so two vertices of the tree need not have an upper bound inside T'. Lemma 3.6 is stated for a direct system (and its proof uses that a map from a finite-dimensional module factors through some F_i, which is only valid for filtered colimits). The key step of the main theorem therefore does not follow from the stated lemma.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Introduction vs. Notation / Proposition 3.9
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims the result for "the category of finitely generated modules over an artinian ring" (repeated in the Introduction: "every join-irreducible torsionfree class in the category of finitely generated modules over an artinian ring is determined by some brick"), but the Notation section fixes Λ to be "a finite-dimensional k-algebra over some field k" and the actual main result (Proposition 3.9) is stated and proved only for Λ-mod of finite-dimensional modules (arguments repeatedly use finite dimension, e.g. "As S is a finite-dimensional module", "the poset of objects smaller than F₃ has finite height"). The claimed generality exceeds what is set up and proved.

The proof says: "Using the fact that torsion classes are closed under quotients, this task can be reduced to proving that every maximal quotient of F is a torsion module", and then works with a simple SUBmodule S ⊆ F and the quotient F/S. A maximal quotient (= simple quotient) being torsion does not imply all proper quotients are torsion; closure under quotients goes the other way. What is actually needed (and what the argument provides) is that F/S is torsion for every simple submodule S, together with the unstated fact that over an artinian ring every non-zero submodule contains a simple submodule. The stated reduction is therefore incorrect/mislabelled.

References [1] (the silting/cosilting survey), [2] (used for Lemma 3.3 "[2, Lemma 2.3]" and Proposition 3.5 "[2, Theorem 3.6]") and [3] (the Barnard–Carroll–Zhu paper underlying Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 2.10) are cited in the text but do not appear in the reference list, which begins at [4]. Conversely, [4] (Crawley-Boevey) and [5] (Demonet–Iyama–Jasso) are listed but never cited anywhere in the text, suggesting mis-numbered or missing bibliographic data.

Theorem 3.1 ("When R is a left noetherian ring, there is a bijection tors(R) ↔ Cosilt(R)") is a non-trivial known result, but it is stated with no reference at all, in contrast to Theorems 3.2, 2.5 and Lemma 3.3 which are attributed. The uncited Crawley-Boevey reference [4] appears to be the intended (missing) attribution.

The proof concludes "it must be that B ∈ cogen(v ∪ w) that is B ∈ v or B ∈ w". This implication is not immediate: cogen(v ∪ w) is defined as the class of objects embedding into a FINITE COPRODUCT of objects of v ∪ w, and cogen(v ∪ w) ≠ cogen(v) ∪ cogen(w) in general. One needs the extra (unstated) argument that, B being f-simple, each component of the embedding B → V ⊕ W is zero or a monomorphism, so B embeds into a single object of v or of w.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proposition 3.9 (statement and last line of proof)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The statement asserts "f = F(B) ∩ Λ−mod" but the notation F(B) is never defined anywhere in the paper (only F for a cosilting torsionfree class, and cogen/filt for closures). Moreover, the final line "So we obtain that f = F(B) ∩ Λ−mod by Theorem 2.5" only justifies the inclusion f ⊆ F(B) ∩ Λ−mod (every f-simple embeds into B, and f = filt(simp f)); the reverse inclusion is simply asserted without proof.
